items.title: If the database query gets faster, how much does checkout actually improve?
items.description: Network (300ms), server processing (800ms), and rendering (600ms) stay fixed — only the database query time changes here, since it's the piece decomposition identified as worth attention. Drag the slider to see how much of checkout's total time the query still accounts for as it gets optimized, and where the point of diminishing returns is.
items.compute: const networkMs = 300; const serverMs = 800; const renderMs = 600; const total = networkMs + serverMs + params.dbMs + renderMs; const dbSharePercent = (params.dbMs / total) * 100; return { total, dbSharePercent };

outputs.label: DB query's share of the total
